Job Description

A Reporting Data Analyst, you will drive the reporting and analytics behind our sales and operations planning (S&OP) process for our portfolio of Adventure Sports brands, delivering insights across demand, supply, and inventory — leveraging AI tools embedded throughout how we analyze data and report on it.

You will partner with demand and supply planning, operations, finance, and commercial teams to build dashboards and recurring S&OP deliverables, consolidating large data sets from disparate, fragmented sources that require cleansing and reconciliation into clear narratives on risks, opportunities, and trends. AI fluency is a core requirement: you will be expected to actively use and continuously expand your use of AI tools across the reporting workflow.

This position reports to the Director of S&OP and is based out of our Irvine, CA office.

As the S&OP Data
Analyst,
you will have an opportunity to:

S&OP Reporting & Cadence

Support the monthly and weekly S&OP reporting cycle across demand, supply, inventory, and executive review meetings.
Build, maintain, and distribute recurring reports and dashboards that summarize plan vs. actual performance, forecast accuracy, and key supply chain KPIs.
Prepare clear, executive-ready PowerPoint summaries and pre-reads that highlight trends, risks, and recommended actions.
Maintain reporting calendars, trackers, and QA checklists to ensure on-time, accurate deliverables.

Track forecast accuracy, bias, MAPE, and other planning KPIs across categories, channels, and SKUs.
Monitor inventory health metrics including weeks of supply, excess and obsolete risk, and stockout exposure.
Partner with planning and operations to run root-cause analysis on plan deviations, surface early warnings, and quantify business impact.
Apply AI-assisted analysis to detect anomalies, explain drivers of forecast and inventory variance, and generate plain-language insights from large data sets.

Dashboards, Tools & Data

Design and maintain Power BI dashboards and self-service reporting for supply chain and S&OP stakeholders.
Leverage Microsoft Copilot and other AI tools to accelerate analysis, summarization, and reporting workflows.
Partner with IT and data teams to validate source data, improve data quality, and document reporting logic.
Consolidate, scrub, standardize, and reconcile data from ERP, planning, finance, commercial, and external partner systems into a trusted reporting view.
Identify opportunities to automate manual reporting and reduce cycle time on recurring deliverables, with a strong bias toward AI-driven automation.

Insights & Cross-Functional Collaboration

Translate data into clear insights and recommendations that inform S&OP decisions and operational priorities.
Partner with finance to reconcile operational performance to financial outcomes and forecasts.
Support ad hoc analyses for leadership, including scenario modeling and business case support.
Document standard definitions and reporting playbooks to drive consistency.
Champion AI adoption across the supply chain and S&OP function — share prompts, workflows, and use cases that help peers work faster and smarter.

jobs.title: Gulf Habitat Restoration Specialist
jobs.description:
Entarian is seeking a Gulf Habitat Restoration Specialist to provide technical, programmatic, environmental compliance, outreach, and restoration planning support for the NOAA Office of Habitat Conservation, Restoration Center. This position will support fishery habitat restoration and related NOAA programs and initiatives in the Northern Gulf of America, with an emphasis on wetland and coastal habitat restoration, restoration planning, environmental compliance, and project management.

Duties Include

Support fishery habitat restoration planning and implementation, including the evaluation, identification, prioritization, design, implementation, and monitoring of restoration projects, with particular emphasis on habitats and biological resources of the Northern Gulf of America.
Support restoration projects involving wetlands and coastal habitats, including living shorelines, salt and tidal marshes, oyster habitat, and barrier islands, and apply ecological principles to habitat restoration planning, implementation, and monitoring.
Provide technical and programmatic support for restoration planning and DARRP cases, including coordination with NOAA staff, local partners, state and federal trustees, responsible parties, technical professionals, and other stakeholders to support project development, implementation planning, monitoring, adaptive management, and reporting.
Support project solicitation, review, and tracking activities, including distribution of requests for proposals, review and scoring of proposals, participation in technical review discussions, development of monitoring plans, participation in implementation planning, review of progress reports, and tracking of project accomplishments.
Provide technical management and oversight of trustee or responsible-party restoration projects, including coordination of draft restoration plans, assessment reports, environmental compliance documents, monitoring and evaluation plans, permit requests, project budgets, adaptive management plans, and restoration scaling activities.
Support Natural Resources Damage Assessment (NRDA) restoration planning and related activities, including gathering information from state and federal trustees, supporting case strategy and decisions through literature and expert-opinion research, preparing topic papers, and supporting the identification, selection, planning, and implementation of restoration projects.
Provide programmatic and project management support, including project scheduling, budgeting, tracking project milestones and deliverables, coordinating field activities and subcontractor oversight, and managing multiple concurrent and competing projects and responsibilities.
Develop and support environmental compliance documentation and permitting, including NEPA documentation using established NOAA and CEQ methods and guidance; Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act; and documentation needed to support compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including the Endangered Species Act and Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act.
Coordinate and communicate with federal, state, local, and non-governmental partners and stakeholders, including navigating competing priorities and communicating complex technical and restoration issues.
Develop outreach and communication products, including draft press releases, project fact sheets, briefing packets, maps, story maps, and other materials; and support public meetings, events, and other outreach activities as needed.
Perform data management and reporting activities, including compiling and inputting project data into the Restoration and Conservation Database (RCDB), DARRTS, and other reporting databases; coordinating information requests; and working with the IT team on potential process improvements.
Provide subject matter expert support to other NOAA programs and initiatives, including independent environmental resource and management studies, meeting participation and reporting, document development, engagement with topic experts, and literature reviews.

The position will support activities throughout the Northern Gulf and requires the employee to be located within the Gulf of America region. The contractor may be required to travel for site visits, meetings, workshops, trainings, and conferences.

The salary for this position is approximately $74,000 - 94,000/year.

Minimum Qualifications

Master’s degree in natural resources, environmental science, fisheries, biology, ecology, marine science, or a related field, with a minimum of 8–10 years of specialized professional experience in applicable field activities, methods, and practices.
Knowledge of the habitats and biological resources of the Northern Gulf of America.
Significant experience with fishery habitat restoration and the application of ecological principles to habitat restoration.
Previous restoration project experience involving wetland and coastal habitat restoration, with experience in one or more of the following: living shorelines, salt or tidal marsh restoration, oyster restoration, or barrier island restoration.
Experience with Natural Resources Damage Assessment (NRDA), the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA), and the Oil Pollution Act (OPA).
Knowledge of federal, state, and local regulations related to living marine resources and habitat restoration projects.
Demonstrated ability to perform field monitoring and habitat assessment activities to identify and evaluate habitat restoration projects.
Strong organizational and project management skills, including project scheduling, budgeting, tracking, reporting, and handling multiple concurrent and competing projects and responsibilities.
Demonstrated ability to coordinate effectively with federal, state, local, and non-governmental partners and stakeholders, navigate competing priorities, and communicate complex issues.
Familiarity with Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act.
Experience with government document retention requirements.
Experience working in a litigation-sensitive environment.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Ability to work independently; reliable, self-starter, self-motivated, and detail oriented.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, as well as routine computer use including email, electronic file management, and calendaring.
Willingness for occasional travel throughout the Gulf of America region.
Must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident and be able to pass a background investigation to obtain a security badge to access applicable government systems and facilities.

Desired Qualifications

Extensive experience with living shoreline and salt/tidal marsh restoration.
Experience with oyster habitat and barrier island restoration.
Public speaking and technical writing skills and experience.

Coordinate coral reef restoration activities across NOAA, partner organizations, coral nursery sites, propagation programs, researchers, resource managers, nonprofit organizations, and other stakeholders to support consistent and effective restoration approaches.
Support development and implementation of coral reef restoration coordination plans, best management practices, permitting and authorization requirements, capacity building, technology and methods transfer, and resilience-based recovery strategies.

Plan, execute, and implement small- and large-scale coral restoration actions associated with NRDA cases, including emergency, primary, and compensatory restoration, and support the scaling of Natural Resource Damages to appropriate restoration.

The Senior Environmental Consultant is responsible for the provision of environmental services during an emergency response and on non-ER projects. The Senior Environmental Consultant will typically assume key roles in the field and/or command post, including Project Manager, Project Technical Director, Environmental Unit Lead, or Technical Specialist roles. They will support Onterris ER Leadership in business development and service growth. They may manage and develop a team of Consultants at varying skill levels reporting directly to them. All Senior Environmental Consultants shall maintain a response bag with company issued PPE and appropriate work clothing. This role also requires on-site deployment for emergency response and other environmental projects; and frequent, extended travel.

Provide technical management and oversight of trustee or responsible-party coral restoration projects, including coordination and development of restoration plans, assessment reports, environmental compliance documents, monitoring plans, permit requests, project budgets, adaptive management plans, and restoration scaling activities.
Plan, execute, and implement small- and large-scale coral restoration actions associated with NRDA cases, including emergency, primary, and compensatory restoration, and support the scaling of Natural Resource Damages to appropriate restoration.
Support NRDA restoration planning under the Oil Pollution Act (OPA) and Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA), including coordination with state and federal trustees, project identification and selection, restoration concepts and designs, monitoring and evaluation plans, case strategy, and technical research.
Provide project management support for coral restoration projects, including identifying project milestones, developing and maintaining budgets and schedules, overseeing and tracking progress, coordinating contracting activities, and supporting project implementation and reporting.
Provide field oversight and technical expertise for coral restoration and monitoring activities, including site evaluation, implementation and refinement of monitoring programs, data collection and synthesis, emergency coral restoration, and support for regional coral reef monitoring activities.
Evaluate and synthesize multi-year coral restoration monitoring data, identify data gaps, conduct or support statistical analyses, refine monitoring protocols, and develop technical reports, memoranda, and scientific publications.
Develop and support environmental compliance documentation and permitting, including NEPA Environmental Assessments and documentation supporting Environmental Impact Statements; coordinate with NOAA General Counsel for Natural Resources and applicable regulatory agencies; and support consultation requirements under the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act and Endangered Species Act.

Collaborate and communicate with federal, state, nonprofit, scientific, and other partners to enhance restoration outcomes and effectively navigate complex technical and programmatic issues.

Perform data management and reporting activities, including accurate and timely tracking of project information in RCDB, DARRTS, SharePoint, and other reporting systems; maintaining Administrative Records and case websites; and coordinating information requests and process improvements.

• Identify and mentor potential leaders, greeters, producers, and presenters.
• Co-lead NAMI trainings.
• Train and support virtual program producers and greeters.
• Identify and communicate upcoming training opportunities to leaders and prospective volunteers.
• Support and facilitate data collection and program evaluation tasks.

• Facilitate the NAMI portion of in-school presentations with community partners.
• Engage in storytelling to support programs, including In Our Own Voice, Voices of Hope and Recovery, and Voices of Hope.

• Engage in a CPFS capacity with community peers in NAMI’s 1:1 peer support program and accurately track data and outcomes for these engagements.
• Obtain and maintain all applicable NAMI program leader certifications.
• Lead outreach efforts at community events and with local organizations including colleges and businesses.
• Support the NAMI COS resource and referral line by answering calls and transfers, and assist front desk volunteers with navigating calls, walk-ins and emails.
• Actively participate in the planning and execution of major NAMI community events.

• Proficiency with Zoom and comfort leading in the virtual space
• Ability and desire to become proficient with NAMI data and tracking systems including Canva, Airtable and Bloomerang Volunteer
• Effective communication skills, both written and verbal

Send a resume and cover letter to openings@namicos.org.
